ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: The account’s biggest missed revenue opportunity is in Non-Brand search, where impression share is low (33–35%) primarily due to rank loss (51% lost to rank in both non-brand campaigns) rather than budget. Budgets are not being fully stressed (budget utilization ~61–64%) and lost-to-budget is materially smaller (14–16%), so increasing competitiveness (bids/efficiency/Quality Score) should unlock more auctions before budget becomes the bottleneck.
notable_patterns: Non-brand campaigns hold only ~33–35% search impression share while losing 51% to rank, versus just 14–16% to budget—pointing to ad rank as the dominant limiter.
Budgets don’t look capped: budget utilization is 63.6% (Flights) and 61.4% (Hotels & Packages), consistent with rank limiting delivery before budgets are exhausted.

Quality Score is a differentiator within non-brand: Hotels & Packages has QS 5.1 (lowest in the account) with the same rank loss (51%) as Flights despite Flights having QS 7.7—suggesting creative/LP relevance and auction competitiveness issues are suppressing non-brand scale.

The two in-scope non-brand campaigns account for the majority of missed impressions in the EDA (356,440 Flights; 300,300 Hotels & Packages), making them the only clearly material levers versus Brand/PMax/Retargeting at current levels.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Delivery is constrained mainly by rank: search IS is 33% with 51% lost to rank versus 16% lost to budget, and budget utilization is only 63.6%, indicating you’re not hitting daily limits so much as failing to win auctions.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase auction competitiveness while protecting efficiency: (1) segment top converting routes/destinations and apply higher bids/tROAS loosening on proven terms, (2) expand/refresh RSAs with query-matched headlines and stronger price/value props, (3) tighten keyword-to-ad-to-landing page alignment to sustain QS (already 7.7) and improve expected CTR, and (4) review auction insights for top outrankers and adjust bid strategy targets until lost-to-rank falls materially (e.g., from 51% toward <40%).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: This is the clearest rank/quality issue: search IS is 35% with 51% lost to rank and only 14% lost to budget, while Quality Score is 5.1 (lowest), suggesting relevance/CTR/LP experience is suppressing Ad Rank and limiting scale even before budget is a constraint.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Prioritize Quality Score and Ad Rank fixes before adding budget: (1) restructure by intent (hotels vs packages vs city breaks) to tighten ad/LP relevance, (2) build new RSAs per intent cluster with stronger query coverage and promo messaging, (3) improve landing page speed/content-match for hotel/package queries, (4) add negatives to cut mismatched traffic that depresses CTR/QS, and (5) once rank loss improves, then consider incremental budget since current utilization is only 61.4% and lost-to-budget is secondary (14%).

market_mapping.why_now_summary: Non-brand search demand and competitive spend in travel are rising right now, so staying rank-constrained (51% lost to rank with only ~33–35% IS) means you’re systematically missing a growing pool of high-intent queries. Because the market’s search spend is accelerating (e.g., +22% QoQ in the UK) while your budgets aren’t fully utilized, the fastest way to capture incremental revenue is to improve Ad Rank/Quality Score and bidding competitiveness now—before higher competitor pressure further raises the cost of winning auctions.

supporting_facts.fact: United Kingdom (pilot account market): Search Spend Growth QoQ = 22.0% and Vertical-Avg Impression Share = 40.0% (source page 13).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: A +22% QoQ rise in search spend signals intensifying auction competition right now. With your non-brand campaigns already losing 51% of impressions to rank, delaying Ad Rank/QS fixes risks even more rank loss as competitors push harder. The 40% vertical-average IS also contextualizes your current ~33–35% IS as behind the market—suggesting headroom that can be captured by improving rank (not just adding budget).

supporting_facts.fact: Keyword demand index for “last minute flights europe” grew from 100 (Q4 2025) to 156 (Q3 2026), Growth = 56% (source page 10).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: This is a concrete indicator that high-intent, non-brand flight demand is expanding sharply. When demand surges, the cost of not winning auctions increases—so lowering lost-to-rank via bids/RSAs/landing-page relevance can translate quickly into incremental volume before budgets become limiting.

supporting_facts.fact: Keyword demand index for “flights to spain” grew from 100 (Q4 2025) to 151 (Q3 2026), Growth = 51% (source page 10).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Rapid growth in a destination-flight query cluster means more auctions are available now. With low IS driven by rank loss, improving competitiveness lets you capture that incremental demand immediately rather than ceding it to outranking advertisers.

supporting_facts.fact: Keyword demand index for “budget airline flight deals” grew from 100 (Q4 2025) to 141 (Q3 2026), Growth = 41% (source page 11).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Price/value-oriented non-brand queries are rising—exactly where stronger RSAs (deal/value props) and better QS can lift Ad Rank. Acting now helps you win more of these auctions without first needing major budget increases.

supporting_facts.fact: Horizon Holidays: Spend Share = 16% and Active Creatives = 34; Channels = Search, Social, Video (source page 10).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: A competitor with sizable spend share and high creative throughput indicates active competitive pressure and message testing. If competitors are iterating creatives aggressively while you remain rank-limited (and one campaign has QS 5.1), improving ad relevance/CTR and landing-page alignment becomes time-sensitive to avoid being perpetually outranked.

supporting_facts.fact: Search: Share of Category Spend = 41% (source page 13).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Search is a large share of category spend, so performance gains from fixing rank constraints in non-brand search can have outsized revenue impact. Given your budgets are not fully stressed, investing effort in Ad Rank/QS improvements is the most immediate lever to capture more of this spend-driven demand.

email_copy.subject: GBP 316,559 sitting behind 47.0% lost-to-rank in your non-brand search
email_copy.hook: Your paid search account isn’t bumping into budget as much as it’s simply not winning enough auctions: impression share is 37.84% while 47.0% is being lost to rank (vs 15.2% to budget). With a daily budget of GBP 6,200, there’s room to scale—if we raise Ad Rank first.
why_now_bullets: UK travel search competition is heating up: Search spend is up 22.0% QoQ, which typically makes rank losses worse for accounts already constrained by position.
High-intent non-brand demand is expanding fast: “last minute flights europe” demand index rose 56% (100 → 156), meaning more auctions are available right now—if you can win them.
You’re behind the vertical benchmark: travel’s average impression share is 40.0%, while your account is at 37.84%—headroom that’s primarily unlocked by improving rank, not just adding budget.
email_copy.stat_sub: Unlocked by reducing rank loss in non-brand search (before budgets become the bottleneck)
email_copy.impact_line: GBP 316,559 is the estimated upside available this quarter if we improve non-brand auction competitiveness—specifically by reducing the 47.0% lost-to-rank through tighter query-to-ad-to-landing-page relevance and bid strategy adjustments that win more high-intent impressions without needing to max out spend first.
email_copy.scope_intro: I’d focus the work where the missed impressions are concentrated: the two non-brand search campaigns driving the majority of rank-related leakage.
email_copy.fix_title: Quick rank-first plan (no budget increase required to start)
email_copy.fix_body: Can you do Tuesday 10:30 or Thursday 14:00 to walk through a rank-first action plan (ad/landing-page relevance + bid/target adjustments) and align on what “good” looks like for impression share and lost-to-rank over the next 2–3 weeks? If neither works, just reply “times” and I’ll send two alternatives.
email_copy.ps: If you’re already planning creative or landing-page updates for peak travel periods, this is the ideal moment to align them to the highest-volume non-brand intent clusters so the Quality/Ad Rank lift shows up immediately in delivery.
